agents.name: manager
agents.system_message: A human manager. They will dictate the task and test finished drafts

agents.name: planner
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the managers request. 
        Your job is the planner. When presented with a request, first try to understand what the manager is asking. Do this by explaining in more detail what the manager is asking for, and what the main challenges will be. Be specific and concise.

        Next, you should develop a plan to solve the request. Explain what will need to be done, and why, in the app. Have a logical order - this will be passed on to the programmer as a settled plan.

        Here is an example of what a settled plan would look like for a request:

        -----------

        The manager has asked us to {the managers request}.

        In other words, what the manager is asking for is {more complete request definition/explanation}

        This means, we need to {expand on functional requirements}


        A successful app for this task must achieve these things:
        1. Functionality/Feature 1
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 1 
        2. Functionality/Feature 2
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 2 
        3. Functionality/Feature 3
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 3 

        Do you agree, manager?

        ------------

        Nice and short and succicnt, while still having the necessary information. Please use this as a guide.

        Work with the manager until the manager approves of the plan. The manager will approve of the plan by using the phrase "sounds good"

        Once the manager said "sounds good", you can write a call to write_settled_plan to write the settled plan into memory. Do not alter the plan after manager approval. Simply remove the question, "Do you agree, manager?".

agents.name: programmer
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the managerss request. Your job is the coder. You will be presented with a plan consisting of the necessary features and functional components. You will produce a python script which attempts to accomplish all of the tasks. However, some tasks are harder than others, and it may be best to leave a comment about what should be there, or what needs to be done. This is an iterative process, so you can expect a chance to revisit the code to fill in the blanks. You do not need to do everything on the first try. If you believe a section of code will be too hard to figure out on the first time, please consider leaving a note that can be tackled on the next iteration.
            
            Do not participate in any conversation or dialog. Your only output should be well formatted code blocks, and nothing else. It is someone elses job to review.
            
            You are only to produce code-blocks. Do not preempt the code with any extra text, and do not add any after it.

agents.name: reviewer
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the items set out in the plan. You are the reviewer. 
        You will review the managers request, the planners interpretation of the request, the approved plan, and the latest code iteration.

        Read through the code, and explain what you see in the code. Explain what look like it should work OK, as it relates to the request and plan.

        If there are errors, the code will go through another iteration. If you believe there are errors, to help guide the programmer, explain what is not OK, and why it is not OK.

        Do not write any code. Just explain in easy to understand terms.

        Your job is critical - please be logical, focus, and try your best.

requirements.description: The system must implement a two-phase workflow: a planning phase that produces a written project plan, and an iterative coding phase that cycles through Coder and Reviewer until the user terminates the program.
expected_behavior: In the planning phase, the manager chats with the planner until the plan is approved
The plan is saved to a project folder via the write_settled_plan tool
The iteration phase begins automatically after the planning chat ends
Each iteration consists of a Coder chat followed by a Reviewer chat
The latest script and comments (if any) are presented at the start of each chat
The loop continues indefinitely until the user terminates the program
negative_cases: The system provides no graceful exit mechanism; termination must be performed externally

requirements.description: Manager agent must be decorated with the write_latest_iteration and write_settled_plan tools so it can execute tool calls on behalf of other agents.
expected_behavior: The manager is a UserProxyAgent that can execute tool calls when prompted by the planner or other agents
negative_cases: If the manager does not have these tools registered, the planner cannot save the plan and the coder/reviewer cannot persist scripts/comments

requirements.description: Planner must call write_settled_plan after manager approval and must not alter the plan afterward.
expected_behavior: Planner presents a numbered plan to the manager
When manager says 'sounds good', planner initiates a tool call to write_settled_plan
After the tool call succeeds, planner confirms completion
Planner must not modify the plan after manager approval
negative_cases: Planner adds extra text or modifies the plan after approval
Planner fails to recognize 'sounds good' as the approval phrase

requirements.description: Coder must output only well-formed Python code blocks, without extra conversational text.
expected_behavior: Coder receives the plan and optionally the latest script/comments
Coder produces a Python code block as its sole output
Coder does not engage in dialogue or provide explanations
negative_cases: Coder includes explanatory text before or after the code block
Coder absentmindedly participates in conversation instead of generating code

requirements.description: Reviewer must produce a textual evaluation and list of criticisms, without generating code.
expected_behavior: Reviewer receives the plan and the latest script
Reviewer explains what looks correct and what is problematic
Reviewer does not write any code
negative_cases: Reviewer provides only vague praise without concrete issues

requirements.description: The system must support resuming an existing project by loading the latest plan, script, and comments from the project folder.
expected_behavior: On restart, the program lists existing projects and offers the option to continue one
Continuing a project immediately starts an iteration with the Coder, presenting the saved plan and latest files
negative_cases: Resume functionality silently fails when project directory structure is corrupted

requirements.description: During the iteration phase, the manager must be able to provide ad-hoc feedback to the Coder/Reviewer before typing 'exit' to finalize the current turn and move to the next agent.
expected_behavior: Manager can test the latest script and report issues to the Reviewer or Coder
Agents must incorporate the feedback in the same turn before the chat ends
The conversation only advances to the next agent when the manager types 'exit'
negative_cases: Coder/Reviewer ignores feedback given during the chat
The system auto-progresses without waiting for 'exit'

requirements.description: The system must persist script files as script_v<n>.py and comment files as comments_v<n>.txt, incrementing the version number with each iteration.
expected_behavior: Coder output is saved to script_v1.py, script_v2.py, etc.
Reviewer output is saved to comments_v1.txt, comments_v2.txt, etc.
Version numbers increment automatically based on existing files
negative_cases: Version numbering conflicts when files are manually added
Tool writes to an incorrect directory due to missing project folder setup

requirements.description: Only the latest script and comment files are presented to agents at the start of each chat, preventing distraction from outdated versions.
expected_behavior: When iteration n begins, the Coder sees only script_v<n-1>.py and comments_v<n-1>.txt (if they exist)
The Reviewer sees only script_v<n>.py and comments_v<n-1>.txt
Older versions are never injected into the context
negative_cases: Program logic accidentally presents all historical files, overwhelming context
Agent retrieves the wrong file version due to naming drift

functions.name: get_number
functions.docstring: Get a valid number from user input.

semantic_graph_review.semantic_graph_review: This system implements a two-phase iterative coding workflow with four agents and two primary tools. The message edges are plausible for a sequential, manually‑driven sequence where the manager initiates one-to-one chats with the planner, then the programmer, then the reviewer. However, the absence of return edges (e.g., reviewer → manager or programmer → manager) and the absence of any agent‑to‑agent edges that might represent an automatic loop are notable. In the analyzed code, however, the iteration is managed by an explicit while‑loop in main.py, so the edges are sufficient to represent the static structure.

suspected_risk_points.evidence: In the agent‑tool‑links, only the manager has the write_latest_iteration and write_settled_plan tools. The requirements state that the manager must execute tool calls on behalf of other agents, which is consistent with the UserProxyAgent pattern. The tool schemas are modeled with empty parameters in the profile, which could indicate missing or inferred parameter definitions. However, in the actual code, these tools accept arguments (e.g., the plan text, the code script). If the model registry used at runtime does not accurately reflect the required parameters, the planner or coder could fail to correctly instruct the manager to invoke the tool. This is a tool‑schema risk.

Similar to write_settled_plan, the write_latest_iteration tool is modeled with no parameters, but the actual implementation expects the code or comment text to be persisted. An incomplete schema could cause the agent to omit required arguments, leading to silent failures or incorrect versioning.
